outcome: No event after 26 January 2024 settles whether every strongly mixing system is strongly 3-mixing for single transformations. Post-window results are restricted: Kanigowski–Ravotti (Oct 2024) prove mixing of all orders for LUS flows (R-actions, not transformations); Wang (Jun 2025, current title on nilmanifolds) gives a quantitative statement for nilmanifold automorphisms; Ryzhikov (Jul 2026) re-proves Kalikow's rank-one theorem via joinings. Surveys dated Apr, May and Nov 2024 and Jul 2026 restate the problem as open. The only counterexample found (Ledrappier, 1978) is for Z²-actions, so it does not decide the Z-question.
problem_asks: Whether every strongly (2-fold) mixing measure-preserving system (T, μ) is strongly 3-mixing. Unpacked: (1) a universal claim over all systems; the bullet does not restrict to Z-actions (single transformations), and the classical question is for Z; (2) the hypothesis, strong mixing: μ(A ∩ Tⁿ B) → μ(A)μ(B) as n → ∞; (3) the conclusion, strong 3-mixing: for sets A₀, A₁, A₂ (and shifts m₁, m₂ → ∞) the joint intersection measure tends to the product of the three measures. The bullet text does not settle whether 3-mixing counts three sets or four (A₀…A₃, as in the Ryzhikov k-fold convention); this is flagged in disputes. (4) A yes/no answer: a proof settles the implication, a counterexample refutes it. Context only, not part of the bullet's question: the bullet's title 'multiple mixing' and the wider literature ask whether mixing implies k-fold mixing for every k ≥ 3, and the bullet asks only the k = 3 case.

events.what_happened: Valery V. Ryzhikov, 'Multiple mixing in ergodic theory' (arXiv:2404.06476, Russian-language). Discusses Rokhlin's 1949 k-fold mixing invariants and the open problem. The abstract says 'We discuss this long time open problem' and claims no new theorem. The ar5iv HTML rendering I read says the problem 'remains open' and restates Ledrappier's Z²-example as 'mixing of multiplicity 3 but not multiplicity 4' (see disputes). That text contains no 'Conjecture 3.1' and no Thouvenot zero-entropy reduction.
events.delivers: Nothing that settles the question. Restates the open problem and the Z²-action counterexample.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.doubts: The ar5iv text was read through an automated rendering, so its statements are as read, not checked against the Russian original. The multiplicity-3/4 statement for Ledrappier's example conflicts with the 2-fold/3-fold statements in other sources (see disputes).
events.direction: Neutral. States the question is open and cites a Z²-action example as showing failure for group actions, not for single transformations.

events.what_happened: Valery V. Ryzhikov, 'Unsolved problems on joinings, multiple mixing, spectrum, and rank' (arXiv:2405.03641, 19 pages, Russian). A problem note that recalls famous open problems. The abstract says that if a hypothetical automorphism with Lebesgue spectrum, infinite rank and no multiple mixing existed, and its spectrum were simple, this would solve the Banach, Rokhlin and del Junco–Rudolph problems; it calls such an example 'seems unlikely'.
events.delivers: No result. A conditional remark: a counterexample of one specific type would answer the problem negatively for that type.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.doubts: None beyond the note being a problem list. The hypothetical example is described, not constructed.
events.direction: Conditionally against yes: a hypothetical Lebesgue-spectrum, infinite-rank example without multiple mixing would be a counterexample. The author says such an example 'seems unlikely'.
events.object: None exhibited. The abstract describes a hypothetical automorphism in a class with Lebesgue spectrum and infinite rank that lacks multiple mixing.

events.what_happened: Adam Kanigowski and Davide Ravotti, 'Multiple mixing for parabolic systems' (arXiv:2410.13686, 74 pages). Introduces locally uniformly shearing (LUS) systems and proves that all LUS flows are mixing of all orders. Shows that mixing smooth flows on surfaces and smooth time-changes of unipotent flows are LUS, and defines a quantitative version: polynomially mixing and polynomially LUS systems are polynomially mixing of all orders. As consequences, Kochergin flows on the torus (for almost every irrational frequency) and smooth time-changes of unipotent flows are polynomially mixing of all orders. Read from the arXiv abstract page; the full text was not readable to me.
events.revisions: v1 only, 17 Oct 2024; no journal reference on the arXiv page I read.
events.delivers: Positive answer, for the class of LUS flows, that mixing implies mixing of all orders. The listed flow classes (mixing smooth flows on surfaces, which by the LUS theorem would follow as an inference from the abstract; smooth time-changes of unipotent flows; Kochergin flows) are covered in the polynomial version as stated. The result concerns flows (R-actions), not transformations (Z-actions).
events.remains: All transformations (Z-actions), and any mixing flow or system outside the LUS class. The question as the bullet states it is not answered for transformations.
events.doubts: The class is flows, so it does not decide the transformation question. A search excerpt reports the authors calling the consequence a positive answer for 'hyperbolic systems'; I could not confirm this because the full text was unreadable, and the abstract says parabolic. The 'LUS implies mixing of all orders' theorem was read from the abstract only.
events.direction: Toward yes (mixing implies mixing of all orders) for the classes it covers. No counterexample in its scope.

events.what_happened: Valery V. Ryzhikov, 'Multiple mixing, 75 years of Rokhlin's problem' (arXiv:2411.07234, math.DS, survey). Abstract: Rokhlin's 1949 k-fold mixing invariants; 'Does mixing imply k-fold mixing?'; 'this problem remains open'; 'We recall shortly some results and discuss related problems.' The HTML render I read lists positive results with citations (Host 1991; Marcus 1978; Ryzhikov 1991; Mozes 1992; Starkov 1993; Ratner 1983; Fayad–Kanigowski 2016; Ryzhikov–Thouvenot 2006; Kalikow 1984; Ryzhikov 1993; Leonov 1960; King 1992; Ryzhikov 2000) and Ledrappier's Z²-action counterexample. It claims no new settlement.
events.delivers: No new settlement. A survey of known partial results: mixing implies k-fold mixing for singular-spectrum automorphisms, several unipotent and Ratner-property flow classes, positive-local-rank flows, quasi-simple flows, finite-rank automorphisms, and Gaussian mixing automorphisms. Counterexample only for Z²-actions.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, including the Z case.
events.doubts: The PDF was unreadable to me, so statements come from the HTML render. The HTML render contains no Thouvenot zero-entropy reduction (Thouvenot is cited only in the Ratner-property discussion), even though a search excerpt attributes such a reduction to this survey. The survey is by an expert but verifies nothing new.
events.direction: No change: states the question is open. Its counterexample is for Z²-actions only.

events.what_happened: Zhenqi Jenny Wang, arXiv:2506.08392. First posted 10 Jun 2025 (v1 title per a search excerpt: 'Multiple mixing and fractional cohomological equation'). Current title: 'Multiple Fractional Cohomological Equations and Quantitative Mixing on Nilmanifolds' (v3, 17 May 2026). The current abstract introduces multiple fractional cohomological equations, claims exponential decay of order-two correlations under partial regularity, 'quantitative mixing of all orders (a quantitative Rokhlin theorem)', and that irrational automorphisms exhibit super-exponential mixing of all orders for C^∞ observables. Single author; the systems are automorphisms of nilmanifolds.
events.revisions: v1 10 Jun 2025 (title then, per search excerpt, 'Multiple mixing and fractional cohomological equation'); v2 11 Jun 2025; v3 17 May 2026 (current). I could not check whether v1 already carried the mixing-of-all-orders claim, so the date may belong to a later version.

Restricted to that algebraic class. The abstract does not say it answers the question for all strongly mixing systems.
events.remains: Every system outside the nilmanifold-automorphism class, and the qualitative question for general strongly mixing systems. Whether the nilmanifold result is new relative to the known mixing of all orders for ergodic group automorphisms is not established by me.

The title and claims changed between versions per the search excerpt and the page. No journal reference or referee report found. The full text was unreadable to me.

Presented as a negative answer to a question of Thouvenot recorded by Iwanik. The abstract does not mention mixing.

events.what_happened: Valery V. Ryzhikov, 'Around Kalikow's theorem on multiple mixing' (arXiv:2607.11852; v2 14 Jul 2026). Abstract: 'Some results in ergodic theory on joinings and multiple mixing'; discusses 'the proof of Steve Kalikow's theorem on 3-fold mixing of 2-fold mixing rank one automorphisms'. Main theorem (Section 3, HTML render): if T is a mixing rank-one transformation and ν is a pairwise independent self-joining of order 3 whose two-dimensional faces are μ×μ, then ν = μ×μ×μ. The page does not label this as new; it credits Kalikow's theorem to Kalikow's 1984 paper. A conditional remark: a counterexample with simple spectrum would solve the Banach and Rokhlin problems.
events.delivers: The rank-one case: for mixing rank-one transformations, a pairwise independent 3-self-joining is product, which by joinings gives 3-fold mixing. This is a re-proof of Kalikow's known rank-one theorem. Restricted to rank-one transformations. Nothing for general mixing systems.
events.remains: All non-rank-one mixing systems, and the general question.
events.doubts: Whether any part is new is not stated. A search excerpt mentions a 'Di(ν) > 0' condition that I could not find in the HTML render. Whether this is a new proof or an exposition is not settled by the text I read.
events.direction: Toward yes, for the rank-one class only (Z-actions).

events.what_happened: Minos Axenides, Emmanuel Floratos, Stam Nicolis, 'Exponential mixing of all orders for Arnol'd cat map lattices' (arXiv:2401.08521). Claims that Arnold cat map lattice field theories are exponentially mixing to all orders; proves l-fold mixing for l = 3, 4, 5, … by an explicit recursive construction of correlation functions; relates this to Rokhlin's conjecture (2-fold implies l-fold for l > 2); states that 2-fold exponential mixing is necessary but not sufficient. The abstract page says it concerns a lattice field theory, not a single measure-preserving transformation.

events.direction: Toward yes (mixing implies all orders) in its own lattice setting. Not a counterexample in any setting.

events.what_happened: One manuscript, 'Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for one transformation' (dated 23 September 2026; the only manuscript in this family). Its main theorem (introduction, thm:main) says: if T is an invertible measure-preserving transformation with measurable inverse on an arbitrary probability space (no standardness or countable-generation assumption) and T is mixing, meaning mu(A cap T^{-n}B) -> mu(A)mu(B) as |n| -> infinity, then for every k >= 3 and all measurable A_1,...,A_k, mu(A_1 cap T^{-n_1}A_2 cap ... cap T^{-(n_1+...+n_{k-1})}A_k) -> product of mu(A_i) as min(n_1,...,n_{k-1}) -> infinity through positive integers. The manuscript counts order by the number of sets (order k = k sets, which it says is multiplicity k-1 in Rokhlin's and Ryzhikov's convention). The proof is by contradiction on a least failing order k. Section 2 extracts a zero-entropy mixing finite-alphabet shift with centred one-site functions that witness a nonvanishing k-fold correlation along diverging layouts. Sections 3-6 build a saturated ordered array object, an operator description of exact lines, measurable labels grouped into finite blocks, and a one-dimensional cancellation result (Proposition orbit-cancellation) that makes the Cesaro averages of the block coefficients vanish. Section 7 integrates these to contradict a constant positive block integral. Section 8 (Corollary, endomorphisms and flows) extends the conclusion to (1) non-invertible measurable endomorphisms on arbitrary probability spaces, for forward times only, and (2) real-time flows whose Koopman operators are strongly continuous on L^1.
events.delivers: Answers the bullet's question affirmatively for a single invertible measure-preserving transformation (a Z-action, the classical setting) on any probability space: every strongly (2-fold) mixing system is strongly 3-mixing, and in fact mixing of every order k >= 3. Order 3 in the manuscript is three sets, which matches the bullet's A_0, A_1, A_2 reading; the all-k statement also covers the four-set (A_0,...,A_3) reading. Restrictions: (a) convergence is along layouts whose successive gaps tend to infinity, i.e. min(n_1, n_2) -> infinity for three sets with n_1 = t_2 - t_1 and n_2 = t_3 - t_2, with t_1 = 0 by invariance. This is the gap form the introduction uses to define mixing of order k. The manuscript does not state a condition that each shift diverges separately, so the bullet's phrase 'shifts m_1, m_2 -> infinity' is ambiguous here and the manuscript's statement is the gap form. (b) The hypothesis is two-sided mixing, which for invertible T is the bullet's strong mixing. (c) The manuscript says Theorem thm:main 'answers Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem affirmatively for one transformation', and its abstract says the same. Its framing (whether ordinary mixing alone implies the next order) matches the bullet in substance. The endomorphism and flow corollaries go beyond the bullet: they cover non-invertible maps, and flows (R-actions) only under an extra L^1 strong-continuity hypothesis.
events.remains: If the claim is correct, nothing remains of the bullet's question for single invertible transformations. Outside it: (i) multi-generator actions (Z^d or other groups). The introduction says the one-generator distinction is essential and cites Ledrappier's zero-entropy mixing Z^2 example, which is not threefold mixing. (ii) For flows, the continuity hypothesis is assumed, not proved, and the text treats it as automatic only for jointly measurable flows on standard probability spaces (cited). (iii) For endomorphisms, only forward times are covered.

machine_checked.scope: Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem asks whether ordinary mixing of one invertible probability-preserving transformation implies mixing of every finite order. The formalization proves this implication. For each $k\ge3$ and every $k$ measurable sets, the measure of their translated intersection tends to the product of their measures as all successive time gaps tend to infinity.

events.doubts: The text flags no step as sketched or conjectural, and the main claim is not hedged. Points a reader should check: (1) Several steps are closed by 'the same argument', 'similarly', or 'the analogous assertion holds with rows and columns exchanged' (for example the common-exact-lines proposition and the incident-operator claim in Section 4, and the first-factor replacement in Section 2), so part of the verification is left to the reader. (2) The proof of Proposition orbit-cancellation (Section 6) is a short case assembly that relies on lemmas stated just before it, and the dissociated case depends on an entropy lemma whose hypothesis H_n = o(n) is checked only afterwards, via a progression-word estimate. (3) The no-standardness claim in the introduction depends on the Section 2 reduction to a finite-alphabet factor. Section 2 opens by saying it places the failure 'in a standard probability space', and the conventions say standardness is obtained only after passing to that factor. (4) The array construction is deliberately asymmetric: row independence is explicitly not asserted (Section 3), and the argument handles the other axis by permuting groups. (5) The main theorem is long (about 3,100 lines of TeX over eight sections). The abstract matches the theorem's statement.; conditional on: None for the main theorem beyond its stated hypotheses (invertible, measure-preserving, mixing). The proof uses standard background results (conditional-expectation convergence, the entropy chain rule, the spectral theorem for compact positive operators) and refers outward at a few steps. The saturation construction in Section 3 follows the 'method of sated extensions' of Austin, cited to a preprint version (its proof of Theorem 3.11 and Lemma 3.12) and not reproduced in full. The exponential-moment estimate for dissociated characters is cited to Green (2002, Section 2.2, Proposition 17), and the manuscript gives the projective-character version itself. The endomorphism corollary uses the natural extension of a standard factor (Rokhlin 1960, Section 9). The flow corollary assumes strong continuity of the Koopman operators on L^1; the text says this holds for jointly measurable flows on standard spaces, citing Rokhlin 1960, Section 1.7. No other manuscript in this family is used.
events.direction: proves the conjecture (affirmative: mixing implies mixing of every order k >= 3 for one invertible transformation)

events.what_happened: None of the four manuscripts claims or proves that strong mixing implies strong 3-mixing. The link is a dependency on a companion. 'Pointwise Multiple Ergodic Averages for Mixing Transformations' (MEA) and 'Pointwise convergence of fourfold ergodic averages for mixing transformations' (fourfold) both take as an input Theorem 1.1 of the companion 'Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for one transformation' (MixingCompanion, dated September 23, 2026; not in this family, not read). As the family restates it (MEA, build/sections/inputs.tex; fourfold, build/sections/02-structure.tex, eq. all-orders-input): for an invertible mixing probability-preserving T, any fixed s≥2, bounded g_1,...,g_s and integer times t_1,...,t_s, the integral of the product of g_j(T^{t_j}x) tends to the product of the integrals as min over i≠j of |t_i−t_j| tends to infinity. MEA's introduction calls this 'the assertion of Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem'. MEA uses it for all orders in its arbitrary-length selected-law argument (build/sections/channels.tex, correlation decay); the fourfold paper does the same (build/sections/05-channels.tex). What each manuscript itself proves: (1) MEA: for every n≥2 and bounded f_1,...,f_n, the averages (1/N) times the sum over k=1..N of the product of f_j(T^{jk}x) converge a.e. to the product of the integrals, along all positive integers N, for invertible bimeasurable mixing T on an arbitrary probability space, with no mixing rate. (2) Fourfold: the same for the times n,2n,3n,4n and four bounded functions. (3) 'Triple ergodic averages with distinct integer slopes': for three bounded functions at any three pairwise distinct nonzero integer slopes, positive or negative, the averages converge a.e. to the product of the integrals, under mixing. (4) 'Pointwise convergence of triple ergodic averages for mixing transformations': the times n,2n,3n, a.e. on an arbitrary probability space with measurable inverse. Manuscripts (3) and (4) identify their limits using only two-function mixing (build/sections/transfer.tex, 'Identifying the limit by mixing', in (3); the Cesàro lemma in build/paper/sections/ergodic.tex in (4), an induction on pairwise correlations). Neither cites MixingCompanion.
events.delivers: Nothing that settles Rokhlin's question. The family makes no 3-mixing claim of its own. Its bearing is conditional: MEA and the fourfold paper rely on the companion's all-orders statement, and no other manuscript in the family does. The companion's restated form covers the k = 3 case only in the min-gap sense: μ(A0 ∩ T^{-t2}A1 ∩ T^{-t3}A2) → μ(A0)μ(A1)μ(A2) as min(|t2|, |t3|, |t2−t3|) → ∞. The list's wording is different. It asks for convergence as the shifts m1 and m2 tend to infinity, with no condition on m1 − m2. The restated form does not cover shift pairs with m1 − m2 bounded, so as written it is weaker than the list's wording. The restated form is the usual k-fold mixing definition and covers all s, so it goes beyond the three-set case the list asks about.
events.remains: Nothing of the problem is settled by this family itself. If the companion's Theorem 1.1 holds in the restated form, the min-gap version of the k = 3 case follows from it. That is the companion's claim, not this family's, and I did not assess it. The list's literal form (m1, m2 → ∞ with no gap condition) is not addressed by the restated companion form. The family's own results are pointwise a.e. convergence statements, not 3-mixing statements.
events.doubts: (a) The theorem statements carry no conditional hypothesis, but the proofs rest on companion results not reproduced here. MEA says 'These companion proofs are not reproduced here.' The fourfold paper says 'The local analytic theorems themselves are cited with their hypotheses and locations.' Manuscript (3) says 'the technical part is a proof by reference to those manuscripts, whereas the ergodic deduction is presented in full', and describes its new estimates as 'extensions of the proofs in H, V, not new proofs of their coefficient-independent projection and row estimates.' (b) Manuscript (4) uses H's uniform local bound at one exponent q in (2,3) and justifies that choice by the parameter order in H's proof. (c) MEA's introduction calls FourfoldCompanion Theorem 1.1 'the fourfold mixing theorem', but in the fourfold manuscript that theorem is a pointwise convergence statement for four functions. (d) The restated companion form and the list's 3-mixing wording differ (see delivers).; conditional on: MEA and the fourfold paper: MixingCompanion Theorem 1.1 in the restated all-orders form above, used for the selected-law and correlation-decay steps; not proved in this family. MEA also takes FourfoldCompanion Prop. 2.2 and Lemma 2.3 (relative structure and relative norm convergence) and SlopesCompanion Prop. 3.5, Lemma 3.6 and Lemma 3.9 (triple oscillation and profile approximation), and cites Austin's sated extensions. The fourfold paper also takes its analytic local estimates from TripleCompanion (manuscript (4) here) and HilbertCompanion ('An L^3 bound for the trilinear Hilbert transform', outside this family). Manuscript (3) takes its local estimates from H (the trilinear Hilbert paper, outside this family) and V (manuscript (4) here). Manuscript (4) takes its local estimate from H.
events.direction: no direct claim on the question; pointwise convergence of multiple averages, conditional on an affirmative companion result

summary: Searched in the frozen problem's terms and in the literature's, and opened every arXiv, journal and survey page I could reach. Across 44 searches, the problem is still stated as open by every source dated after 26 January 2024 that I read: Ryzhikov's April 2024 discussion, his May 2024 problem note, his November 2024 survey, and his July 2026 Kalikow paper (which states the rank-one case, not the general problem). No event after the frozen date settles the question for single transformations. Within the window the progress is restricted to classes: Kanigowski–Ravotti (October 2024) prove mixing of all orders for LUS flows, which include smooth mixing flows on surfaces and smooth time-changes of unipotent flows (flows, not transformations, so the bullet's question is not decided); Wang (June 2025, now titled 'Multiple Fractional Cohomological Equations and Quantitative Mixing on Nilmanifolds') claims a quantitative mixing-of-all-orders statement for nilmanifold automorphisms, with an unexplained overlap comment on arXiv; Ryzhikov's July 2026 paper re-proves Kalikow's rank-one theorem via joinings. Discounted events, each recorded: Hu–Xu–Zhang (July 2026, orbit multiplicity, Thouvenot's other question), Chaika–Robertson (November 2024, minimal self-joinings), Gordillo Herrerías (August 2025, strong mixing of flows on translation surfaces), Auer (May 2026, random systems), Vereshchagina–Ryzhikov (March 2026, infinite measure), and Axenides et al. (January 2024, lattice field theory; ten days before the frozen date). Pre-window partial results are recorded individually: Kalikow 1984 (rank one, 3-fold), Host 1991 (singular spectrum), Ryzhikov 1993 (finite rank and rank one, all orders), del Junco–Yassawi 2000, several flow classes from the survey, the PID-joining papers (Janvresse–de la Rue 2007; Gutman–Huang–Shao–Ye 2016; Ryzhikov 2023), and the zero-entropy reduction (Thouvenot, 1995, not retrieved). Counterexamples found: Ledrappier 1978 for Z²-actions (zero-entropy), and de la Rue's 2004 relative example. The 2006 de la Rue paper, whose title says 3-dot counterexamples are impossible in one dimension, has an abstract that says only 'strong obstacles', a gap the judging pass should weigh. AI involvement: none found. No source I read names an AI system for this problem. The closest AI-disclosed mixing paper I saw, arXiv 2608.29403 ('Kac's Walk on Rotation Matrices Mixes in Θ(n²) Steps: A Proof Discovered with AI'), concerns a Markov chain, not Rokhlin's question, and I saw it only as a search excerpt. The Anthropic, DeepMind and Tao results I searched for named no mixing result. The OpenAI August 2026 'ten results' PDF was unreadable to me, so an AI-lab mixing result there is not excluded. Close calls, both sides: (a) Scope: the bullet does not say Z. Read as all group actions, the answer is already no (Ledrappier, Z²); read as Z, it is open. (b) Flows versus transformations: Kanigowski–Ravotti and Kucharski are about flows. (c) Rank-one 2026 paper: a re-proof of a known case, or new exposition; the text does not say which. (d) Bergelson–Zelada's 'almost' result: a weaker form whose exceptional set I could not read. (e) Wang's nilmanifold result: a new quantitative statement or a restatement of the classical automorphism result, undetermined here. (f) Numbering: whether 3-mixing counts three or four sets, which affects Ledrappier's example (see disputes).
competing_reading: Read 'systems' as all measure-preserving group actions, as the bullet's wording allows. Then the answer is already no by Ledrappier's 1978 Z²-example (2-fold but not 3-fold mixing, zero entropy), and the bullet would be a resolved negative for group actions but still open for Z. Alternatively, read 'strongly 3-mixing' with the Ryzhikov k-fold convention (k+1 sets). Then the Ledrappier example is reported as 3-fold but not 4-fold, which would not be a counterexample at the 3-set level and would change the Z² reading. On the positive side, a reader who counts the flow results (Kanigowski–Ravotti 2024; Kanigowski–Kułaga-Przymus–Ulcigrai 2016) or the nilmanifold result (Wang 2025) as progress on the bullet must accept that flows and algebraic automorphisms fall under 'systems'. A reader who treats Bergelson–Zelada's 'almost' result as progress must accept an exceptional set of times the bullet does not allow.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of Bergelson–Zelada (arXiv 2010.06146): the exact exceptional set, and whether the result covers every sequence tending to infinity for Z-actions. (2) The full text of Ryzhikov 2404.06476 and the 1978 Ledrappier note, to settle the 3-fold versus 4-fold numbering, and whether the bullet's '3-mixing' means three or four sets. (3) Wikipedia's reference [39] for the bullet (not read: the article runs to about 295,000 characters and I read only the first 100,000). (4) Thouvenot's 1995 paper and Kosenko's UBC note (not reachable: the link redirects to a site that does not list it), to confirm the zero-entropy reduction and its direction. (5) The full text of Kanigowski–Ravotti (arXiv 2410.13686) to see whether any transformation or non-LUS class is covered, and whether the 'hyperbolic systems' consequence the search excerpt reports is in the paper. (6) The full text of Ryzhikov 2607.11852, to decide whether the rank-one result is new or a re-proof. (7) The full text of Wang (arXiv 2506.08392) and of math/0512192, to check the overlap comment and whether the nilmanifold result is new. (8) A dated listing of arXiv math.DS for 2025–2026 with 'multiple mixing', 'k-fold mixing' or 'Rokhlin' in the title or abstract, which my searches could not produce reliably. (9) The text of the OpenAI August 2026 'ten results' document and of any AI-lab announcement listing mixing results, to rule out an AI-lab result on this problem.

event.what_happened: One manuscript, 'Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for one transformation' (dated 23 September 2026; the only manuscript in this family). Its main theorem (introduction, thm:main) says: if T is an invertible measure-preserving transformation with measurable inverse on an arbitrary probability space (no standardness or countable-generation assumption) and T is mixing, meaning mu(A cap T^{-n}B) -> mu(A)mu(B) as |n| -> infinity, then for every k >= 3 and all measurable A_1,...,A_k, mu(A_1 cap T^{-n_1}A_2 cap ... cap T^{-(n_1+...+n_{k-1})}A_k) -> product of mu(A_i) as min(n_1,...,n_{k-1}) -> infinity through positive integers. The manuscript counts order by the number of sets (order k = k sets, which it says is multiplicity k-1 in Rokhlin's and Ryzhikov's convention). The proof is by contradiction on a least failing order k. Section 2 extracts a zero-entropy mixing finite-alphabet shift with centred one-site functions that witness a nonvanishing k-fold correlation along diverging layouts. Sections 3-6 build a saturated ordered array object, an operator description of exact lines, measurable labels grouped into finite blocks, and a one-dimensional cancellation result (Proposition orbit-cancellation) that makes the Cesaro averages of the block coefficients vanish. Section 7 integrates these to contradict a constant positive block integral. Section 8 (Corollary, endomorphisms and flows) extends the conclusion to (1) non-invertible measurable endomorphisms on arbitrary probability spaces, for forward times only, and (2) real-time flows whose Koopman operators are strongly continuous on L^1.
event.delivers: Answers the bullet's question affirmatively for a single invertible measure-preserving transformation (a Z-action, the classical setting) on any probability space: every strongly (2-fold) mixing system is strongly 3-mixing, and in fact mixing of every order k >= 3. Order 3 in the manuscript is three sets, which matches the bullet's A_0, A_1, A_2 reading; the all-k statement also covers the four-set (A_0,...,A_3) reading. Restrictions: (a) convergence is along layouts whose successive gaps tend to infinity, i.e. min(n_1, n_2) -> infinity for three sets with n_1 = t_2 - t_1 and n_2 = t_3 - t_2, with t_1 = 0 by invariance. This is the gap form the introduction uses to define mixing of order k. The manuscript does not state a condition that each shift diverges separately, so the bullet's phrase 'shifts m_1, m_2 -> infinity' is ambiguous here and the manuscript's statement is the gap form. (b) The hypothesis is two-sided mixing, which for invertible T is the bullet's strong mixing. (c) The manuscript says Theorem thm:main 'answers Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem affirmatively for one transformation', and its abstract says the same. Its framing (whether ordinary mixing alone implies the next order) matches the bullet in substance. The endomorphism and flow corollaries go beyond the bullet: they cover non-invertible maps, and flows (R-actions) only under an extra L^1 strong-continuity hypothesis.
event.remains: If the claim is correct, nothing remains of the bullet's question for single invertible transformations. Outside it: (i) multi-generator actions (Z^d or other groups). The introduction says the one-generator distinction is essential and cites Ledrappier's zero-entropy mixing Z^2 example, which is not threefold mixing. (ii) For flows, the continuity hypothesis is assumed, not proved, and the text treats it as automatic only for jointly measurable flows on standard probability spaces (cited). (iii) For endomorphisms, only forward times are covered.

machine_checked.scope: Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem asks whether ordinary mixing of one invertible probability-preserving transformation implies mixing of every finite order. The formalization proves this implication. For each $k\ge3$ and every $k$ measurable sets, the measure of their translated intersection tends to the product of their measures as all successive time gaps tend to infinity.

event.doubts: The text flags no step as sketched or conjectural, and the main claim is not hedged. Points a reader should check: (1) Several steps are closed by 'the same argument', 'similarly', or 'the analogous assertion holds with rows and columns exchanged' (for example the common-exact-lines proposition and the incident-operator claim in Section 4, and the first-factor replacement in Section 2), so part of the verification is left to the reader. (2) The proof of Proposition orbit-cancellation (Section 6) is a short case assembly that relies on lemmas stated just before it, and the dissociated case depends on an entropy lemma whose hypothesis H_n = o(n) is checked only afterwards, via a progression-word estimate. (3) The no-standardness claim in the introduction depends on the Section 2 reduction to a finite-alphabet factor. Section 2 opens by saying it places the failure 'in a standard probability space', and the conventions say standardness is obtained only after passing to that factor. (4) The array construction is deliberately asymmetric: row independence is explicitly not asserted (Section 3), and the argument handles the other axis by permuting groups. (5) The main theorem is long (about 3,100 lines of TeX over eight sections). The abstract matches the theorem's statement.; conditional on: None for the main theorem beyond its stated hypotheses (invertible, measure-preserving, mixing). The proof uses standard background results (conditional-expectation convergence, the entropy chain rule, the spectral theorem for compact positive operators) and refers outward at a few steps. The saturation construction in Section 3 follows the 'method of sated extensions' of Austin, cited to a preprint version (its proof of Theorem 3.11 and Lemma 3.12) and not reproduced in full. The exponential-moment estimate for dissociated characters is cited to Green (2002, Section 2.2, Proposition 17), and the manuscript gives the projective-character version itself. The endomorphism corollary uses the natural extension of a standard factor (Rokhlin 1960, Section 9). The flow corollary assumes strong continuity of the Koopman operators on L^1; the text says this holds for jointly measurable flows on standard spaces, citing Rokhlin 1960, Section 1.7. No other manuscript in this family is used.

judgement.why: The statement is Rokhlin's classical question, which is about a single transformation (Z-action); Ledrappier's Z²-example, Bergelson–Zelada's almost-all-times form, relative mixing, random and infinite-measure settings are therefore variants. Class results (rank one, finite rank, singular spectrum, Gaussian, unipotent/Ratner/LUS flows, nilmanifold automorphisms, PID) are cases, since flows and algebraic classes are 'systems' the statement quantifies over. Ryzhikov's 2026 Kalikow paper re-proves a known case and moves nothing, so none. openai-math-145 claims the full implication for every invertible measure-preserving transformation, all orders k ≥ 3 including the three-set reading, in the standard gap formulation of k-fold mixing; that answers the statement in full, so whole. Its only checks are a Lean formalisation (F7) and no human reader, so unreviewed; it is 8 days old with no specific identified error, so credible rather than doubtful. The README quote says the model obtained the results, so generated. openai-math-154 makes no 3-mixing claim of its own and only depends on 145, so none. Pre-snapshot journal papers are counted digested by journal of record; Thouvenot 1995 and Gutman et al. have no venue recorded, so unreviewed.
judgement.doubts: openai-math-145 is a landmark claim on a 77-year-old problem, AI-generated, unread by any human expert, with steps closed by 'the same argument' and the sated-extension machinery cited rather than reproduced; whether the Lean statement OAI.Rokhlin.mixing_all_finite_orders faithfully matches the problem was not checked by anyone and sorry_free is null. The statement's 'systems' could be read to include Z²-actions, under which Ledrappier 1978 would already be a pre-snapshot refutation; I followed the classical Z reading. The 3-vs-4-set numbering is moot for 145 because it proves all orders.
